correctness.rationale: The singular conditions are explicitly solved in every characteristic: ten sign-partition critical points with nondegenerate projective Hessian for characteristic zero or at least five; characteristic-two invariance along the diagonal yields a cubic cone over f=sum_{i!=j} y_i^2 y_j. The derivative coefficient matrix I+J squares to the identity over F2, giving the complete saturated projective Jacobian ideal (y_1^2,...,y_4^2), length 16 and multiplicity three at the vertex. The base Hermitian surface is smooth; a complete F4 plane incidence enumeration finds 27 rational lines, and the classical 27-line bound exhausts all geometric lines, hence all cone planes. Frobenius makes the char-3 cubic redundant. The packaged exact checker reproduces finite cases and incidence; arbitrary characteristic is supported by explicit algebraic proof, not finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Classical ten nodes, Segre power sums, and smooth-cubic 27 lines are not claimed novel. The checked Howard–Millson–Snowden–Vakil sources describe the characteristic-independent graphical construction and ordinary Segre coordinates, including their failure in characteristic three and a coordinate relation requiring division by two, but no complete characteristic-two local Tjurina scheme or Hermitian-plane incidence for the coefficientwise power-sum model. The nearest searchable mathematical records concern other cubic or Hermitian configurations rather than an implication covering the same result. This is a qualified self-review, with explicit unindexed-literature risk.

value.rationale: The object is the natural integral symmetric equation of the classical Segre cubic, and the primes 2 and 3 are structurally dictated by the six-coordinate sum and by Frobenius. The characteristic-two fiber replaces the ordinary ten-node threefold by a normal Hermitian cone with a nonreduced length-16 singular scheme, and an exactly described configuration of 27 planes and 45 intersection lines. This simultaneously quantifies singular-scheme degeneration and a jump in linear subvarieties, and distinguishes it from the dimension-jump at prime three. These motivated geometric invariants and model-dependence information go beyond a cheap congruence check or a standard isolated finite-field count.
